messages:
ashley: Heads-up — we've got a Private customer (EU fin-reg) who says their on-prem boxes block all outbound traffic except to a small allowlist. They want Redwood's control plane to never route traffic outside their permitted regions. Can we model this in routing policies?

 todd: +1. We already have region-based routing, but this is more strict: control-plane must enforce egress-allowed list per org and never fall back to a different region model implicitly.

 vikram: Two constraints I see: 1) control-plane decisions (routing selection) may require connectivity to model stores/kernels in other regions for fallback — that's unacceptable. 2) telemetry/usage reporting needs a path — if they block telemetry we still need billing/quotas enforced.

 sara: For telemetry we could support a push-gateway model: customer ships a relay in their VPC that accepts signed telemetry and forwards to Redwood over an approved egress. That keeps data plane inside their network except for the minimal audit bundle.

 ashley: Proposal: add org-level field: `egress_guardrails.allowed_regions` and `egress_guardrails.block_variant_fallback_outside_regions = true`. Control plane rejects any route that violates this. If no compatible route exists, fail fast with 409 and clear error describing allowed variants.

 todd: UX change in Console/Routes: show a prominent banner on rollout config: "this org enforces egress guardrails — only region X,Y allowed — fallback outside will be blocked". Also add a per-route preview that simulates whether a canary roll will violate guardrails.

 vikram: We also need an internal API contract change: /route/evaluate should accept optional `org_id` and `vpc_profile` flags and return `route_candidates` with `egress_region` and `requires_control_plane_egress: bool`.

 sara: Example response sketch: ```{ "route_candidates": [ {"model":"rwd-3-small-eu","egress_region":"eu-west-1","requires_control_plane_egress":false}, {"model":"rwd-3-generic","egress_region":"us-west-2","requires_control_plane_egress":true} ] }``` But for this org the second candidate must be filtered out server-side.

 ashley: On the fallback strategy: if no same-region variant exists, we should either (A) fall back to a quantized on-prem friendly variant that customers can preload (requires provisioning path), or (B) return an explicit failure to the caller. My vote: default to B, with an opt-in preload for A.

 todd: Agree. Preload option needs ops flow: package + signed manifest, and we should add an entry in Console under Private > Model Assets to upload/approve.

 vikram: Quotas/usage implications: If we can't route to hosted models and the customer uses preloaded variant, usage should be billed at reserved-capacity API metrics, not hosted usage. We should tag telemetry differently: `billing_source = onprem-preloaded` vs `billing_source = hosted`.

 sara: Rollout UX: When creating a rollout you can select "respect org egress policy" checkbox (default on for Private orgs). If a stage would hit a non-compliant route, show red state and block canary promotion.

 ashley: Action items: - vikram: add `egress_guardrails` fields to org API + update /route/evaluate to filter candidates (owner) - todd: console banner + rollout preview + model assets upload flow (owner) - sara: design push-gateway pattern + telemetry tag spec (owner) - me: write product RB with error codes and docs for Sales/SRE (owner)

 deploy-bot: @ashley created task INF-4723: "Org egress guardrails - API and Console" — https://redwood/tasks/INF-4723

 todd: Quick question — should we allow a hybrid mode where control plane can contact other regions for non-sensitive metadata (model schema) but not for serving? That feels risky.

 vikram: I'd avoid partial allowances — customers will interpret "allowed" loosely. Simpler to keep binary: control plane may not cause egress outside allowed regions. Metadata can be synced via customer-provided relay if needed.

 sara: We should update telemetry dashboard to surface `egress_blocked_events` so SRE can help customers debug missing fallbacks.

 ashley: OK let's prototype API change today. I'll ping infra for a short sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
